description: Per-fund facts that Form N-PORT does not carry: net and gross expense ratio, inception, tracked index, the index's own region words and the sponsor-stated mandate. Read from each fund's own SEC-FILED summary prospectus (Form 497K) or registration statement (Form 485BPOS) and committed with a URL, an accession and a date, because a fee or an index can change and a number without a date cannot be rechecked. An SEC filing is used in preference to a sponsor web page for the same reason Experiment 008 did so: a filing has an accession number and is permanently archived, and a web page has neither. This file is an INPUT to the screen, not an output of it, and it contains no price, return or performance data of any kind.
relationship_to_exp_002_facts: The same ProductFacts fields, with the same meanings, so a fee or an inception date is comparable across the two audits. Four fields are additional and ex-US specific: index_region_words, stated_region, converted_from_mutual_fund and mandate_change_tier.

mandate_change_policy.tier_1_excluded: A fund whose stated strategy changed in KIND inside the window is given mandate_change_tier 1, fails the mandate_stable criterion and is recorded rather than graded. It has no single mandate over the window, so there is nothing to grade its exposure against.
mandate_change_policy.tier_2_retained_and_reported: A change of tracked index, index name, index provider or sponsor branding that leaves the strategy intact does NOT exclude a fund. Excluding those would remove most of the shelf and would hide exactly what the rolling-loading stability test exists to find. Every one is recorded below and reported beside the stability results.
mandate_change_policy.the_ishares_stoxx_transition: INTF, ISCF and EMGF all moved from an MSCI Diversified Multiple-Factor index to a STOXX Equity Factor index (INTF on 2022-06-01, ISCF and EMGF on 2023-03-01). Experiment 002 classified this exact change, for INTF, as TIER 1 on the ground that the STOXX quality score incorporates carbon-intensity and greenhouse-gas-target signals that the MSCI index did not use, so the strategy changed in kind and not only in supplier. That classification is carried over here unchanged and applied to all three funds. The alternative reading -- that the objective sentence is verbatim identical before and after, so the change is tier 2 -- is defensible on its own but would grade the same fund one way in the US audit and another way here, and comparability between the two audits is the whole point of this experiment. The decision was taken before any ex-US return was downloaded.

known_gaps: EWX and GWX commencement-of-operations dates are not in their current summary prospectuses; they were read from the sponsor's earlier SEC-filed SAI and registration statement (accessions 0000950135-08-003639 and 0000950135-09-000503).
SCHC, FNDC and TLTD inception dates are likewise not in the current prospectus and were read from each fund's earliest 497K.
MFEM's 0.49% net ratio rests on a contractual waiver running only through 2026-10-31 with a 36-month recoupment provision, so realised expenses can exceed it. The gross 0.50% is recorded beside it.

EFV and EFG management-fee schedules gained lower breakpoint tiers in a 497 filed 2026-07-31 that has not yet been reflected in a reissued fee table, so their filed 0.31% and 0.34% may now be marginally high.

No stated-index RETURN series is available for any fund here. Index levels are licensed products and no free source with a documented contract carries them, so every tracking difference in this experiment is against a constructed benchmark.
